chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Asbat ibn Salim, the seller of al-Zutti, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked one day, while I was with him, about Mu'adh, the seller of karabis (a type of fabric), and it was said that he had left trade. He said, 'The work of Satan, the work of Satan. He who leaves trade loses two-thirds of his intellect. Do you not know that a caravan came from Syria to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he bought from it and traded, and profited from it enough to pay off his debt.'
ai.seo_question: Why is leaving trade considered a loss of intellect in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual and intellectual benefits of commerce by noting that abandoning trade results in the loss of two-thirds of one's intellect. He validates this by citing the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) own engagement in trade with a Syrian caravan to settle his debts, establishing commerce as a dignified means of sustenance and financial independence within Shia jurisprudence.
